newsitem.title: UK: Fancy diamond fans flock to London.
newsitem.headline: Fancy diamond fans flock to London.

text.p: Fans of fancy diamonds from all over Europe flocked to London on Thursday as the world's most sparkling and exclusive roadshow rolled into Britain for the first time.

Australian miners Argyle Diamonds, 60 percent owned by Anglo-Australian mining group RTZ-CRA, have brought their annual multi-billion dollar Pink Diamond Tender to London for two days as part of an annual worldwide tour which takes in Tokyo, Hong Kong and Geneva.
Argyle has invited a select number of international dealers and collectors to examine its 1996 haul of 47 rare pink gems, including two of the largest polished pink diamonds ever sold by the company.

Last year's sale of jewels from Argyle's mine in remote north-west Australia raised more than 4.5 million dollars. With two stones weighing more than three carats on offer this year's could go even higher.
"As fancy coloured diamond connoisseurs appreciate, pink diamonds above three carats in weight are extremely rare," said Argyle's sales manager David Fardon.

"In the 11 year history of Argyle's Pink Diamond Tenders, we have only offered six pink diamonds in this category." Colours of the highly prized gems range from browny pinks at the cheaper end, through purplish pinks and, rarest and costliest of all, stones so saturated with colour they border on red.
Organisers are hoping their display will attract diamond connoisseurs of the calibre of Geneva-based Robert Mouawad, who bought the entire collection in both 1991 and 1993.
